Hi Carlos / Priya,

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on: 

- Product context: interactive recommendations + nightly batch re-ranks.
- Estimated token profile (please confirm): avg ~25M tokens/day, peak bursts to ~75M tokens/day during heavy trading windows; heavy batch runs overnight (~200M tokens/job).
- Primary goal: keep interactive latency good (p95 target for UI flows < 400ms) while hitting an acceptable unit cost. You mentioned a target of roughly $250 / 1M tokens as a reference number.

Options we discussed (high-level):
- Hosted (Balanced tier): streaming + small batching window for interactive paths. Fast time-to-value, no infra commitment.
- Dedicated (Reserved): predictable throughput, aggressive batching + prefix caching, better unit economics for sustained volume. Requires throughput commit.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): lowest unit cost at scale but higher setup/capex and onboarding time.

What I need from you to circle back with a concrete proposal:
1) Confirm the token volumes above (avg/peak/monthly) — I attached token_volume_estimate.xlsx with the numbers we used.
2) Confirm the budget range / target $/1M tokens you can consider (you mentioned ~$250).
3) Confirm latency SLOs by use case (interactive UI vs background batch).

Next steps I propose: once you confirm, I’ll loop in Rishi (solutions) and Vivek (SRE/pricing) to run a unit-economics calc and recommend a bin (Hosted vs Dedicated) and recommended batching/streaming settings. I attached our baseline_latency_report.pdf and the token estimate for reference.

Hi Carlos,

Thanks — helpful. Quick answers to your two questions:

1) Streaming vs short-window batching:
- Streaming (token-by-token output) is usually higher cost per token because it favors lower-latency paths and less batching. It’s ideal for human-facing interactive flows where per-request latency matters.
- Short-window batching (e.g., 50–200ms batch windows) can reduce unit cost materially because we can amortize kernel and memory work across requests; p95 will increase depending on client-side tolerated wait. For your p95 < 400ms target, a small batching window with streaming fallback for tail requests is a good hybrid.

2) Dedicated ballpark at your tiers:
- With sustained avg ~25M/day (750M/month) and peak patterns you described, a 12-mo reserved plan typically moves the unit economics into the ~$180–$230 / 1M tokens range depending on model variant, quantization option, and caching effectiveness.

I'll pull together two concrete options (Hosted Balanced vs Dedicated Reserved) with an example cost sheet and recommended batching/streaming config. Looping in Rishi and Vivek for the detailed calc — we'll also propose a deployment pattern to hit p95 <400ms for interactive flows.

Can you do Aug 6 at 10:00 AM PT? If so, I'll send a calendar invite and include Rishi/Vivek.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Carlos / Priya — following up with two concrete options based on the numbers you shared and our internal calc. See brief summary below and attached cost_breakdown.xlsx & SOW_draft_v1.pdf.

Option A — Hosted (Balanced)
- Unit price: ~$320 / 1M tokens
- Delivery: Streaming for interactive flows + 100ms batching window for consolidation.
- Latency: p95 ~300ms (depending on model variant); consistent out-of-the-box SLA and no infra commit.
- Pros: Fast onboarding, built-in fallbacks and autopolicy routing.
- Cons: Higher unit cost vs reserved capacity.

Option B — Dedicated (12-mo reserved)
- Unit price: ~$210 / 1M tokens (assuming 12-mo commit and expected caching/batching efficiencies)
- Delivery: Dedicated GPU pool, aggressive batching for background jobs, hybrid streaming for interactive with prefix caching.
- Latency: p95 ~250–350ms depending on batch sizing and model selection.
- Pros: Better unit economics at your monthly volumes. Requires throughput commit.

Recommendations and next steps:
1) If your priority is fastest time-to-value and lower operational overhead, we recommend Option A to start and then move to Dedicated once commit thresholds are met.
2) If long-term unit cost is the priority and you can commit, Option B drives meaningful savings at scale.
3) Proposed follow-up: 30-min meeting on Aug 6, 10:00 AM PT with Rishi & Vivek to review assumptions (model choice, quantization, caching %), walk through cost_breakdown.xlsx, and finalize an SOW.

Please confirm the time and we'll send a calendar invite. Once we agree on a path, we’ll generate a targeted SOW and a short technical runbook for the rollout (canary -> A/B -> full).

Thanks,
